item.text: The bounded continuation has now been attempted chapter-by-chapter across 2B–8B. The strongest recoveries are a November 2022 MILF ceasefire and CPP/NDF decision record (2B), contemporaneous security-force accountability and red-tagging evidence (3B), post-election monitoring and institutional checks (4B), household poverty and subsidy evidence (5B–6B), inspectable campaign-finance disclosures and donor-network reporting (7B), and transition/disaster/coordination records (8B). I’m assembling the permissive handoff and manifest fragment now, with unresolved gaps kept as gaps rather than converted into negative evidence.

Continuation completed sequentially for Chapters 2B–8B. No score, range, ranking, or judge-directed advice was assigned. Filesystem writes remained blocked, so the manifest updates are supplied for parent persistence.

## New evidence units

### Chapter 2B — Conflict, peace, and escalation

- **E042** — On July 15, 2022, National Security Adviser Clarita Carlos stated that Marcos had the final decision on resuming CPP–NDF peace talks; local engagement continued, and the NTF-ELCAC proposed amnesty and reconciliation measures. Attribution is authority-based and documents an unresolved policy choice, not a completed peace settlement. Contrary evidence: the talks remained stalled and the NTF-ELCAC and AFP retained counterinsurgency roles. [PNA, lines 65–86](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1179031). Lenses: `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`, `2B.10`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E043** — Following an armed clash between government troops and MILF forces on November 8, 2022, government and MILF mechanisms brokered a ceasefire on November 10. The agreement directed AFP commanders to implement the ceasefire, withdraw reinforcements, register local combatants, and establish a joint AFP–PNP–MILF peace-and-order detachment. This is direct target-period evidence of de-escalation and institutional peace mechanisms, while also documenting a contemporaneous armed incident. [PeaceGovPH, lines 55–83](https://peace.gov.ph/2022/11/govt-milf-sign-ceasefire-agreement-in-basilan/). Lenses: `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`, `2B.10`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

Shortfall: no inspectable ruler-attributed civilian-harm record, proxy or arms-recipient evidence, or security-operation accountability finding was recovered.

### Chapter 3B — Physical integrity and state coercion

- **E044** — The 2022 U.S. human-rights report recorded ongoing police killings, CHR investigations into 111 new alleged extrajudicial or politically motivated killing complaints, 48 drug-related killing investigations, 33 torture cases, and no prosecutions or convictions for extrajudicial killings during the year. It also recorded administrative charges against police personnel but substantial exonerations and continuing impunity. These are target-period national security-force findings; they do not establish Marcos-directed conduct. [U.S. State Department report, lines 43–76](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089246.html). Lenses: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E045** — The same report found the Marcos administration’s position on red-tagging unclear: National Security Adviser Carlos condemned it in June, while Justice Secretary Remulla defended the practice during the November UN review. The NTF-ELCAC remained the primary actor, and red-tagging continued to target activists, unions, religious groups, academics, and media organizations. This provides contrary evidence against treating a stated restraint policy as implemented correction. [U.S. State Department report, lines 160–169](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089246.html). Lenses: `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

Shortfall: no presidential security directive, case-level remedy audit, vulnerable-group protection record, or proof of personal knowledge/tolerance was found.

### Chapter 4B — Political freedom and institutional constraint

- **E046** — NAMFREL’s preliminary election report described the May 2022 election as generally smooth but identified concerns involving automated-election-system transparency and performance, electoral-board training, COVID protocols, and vote-buying reports. This independently supports a mixed election narrative and does not attribute all defects to Marcos personally. [NAMFREL/ANFREL](https://anfrel.org/namfrels-preliminary-report-2022-elections-went-smoothly-but-not-without-issue/). Lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`, `4B.8`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E047** — Executive Order No. 1, issued in 2022, reorganized the Office of the President and abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and Office of the Cabinet Secretary. This is direct presidential institutional action, but its effect on accountability capacity is not established by the order alone. [Senate Legislative Reference Bureau](https://ldr.senate.gov.ph/executive-issuance/executive-order-no-1-s-2022). Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.10`, `8B.2`, `8B.3`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E048** — In September 2022, Malacañang stated that Marcos’s cabinet would attend congressional inquiries and that the president welcomed congressional checking of alleged anomalous transactions. This is favorable procedural evidence, but it records an assurance rather than independently verified compliance or effective legislative constraint. [PNA](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1183078). Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.10`, `8B.8`. Disposition: `context`.

Shortfall: no systematic post-inauguration surveillance record, later-2022 protest-treatment dataset, or succession/term-limit conduct was recovered.

### Chapter 5B — Economic governance and distribution

- **E049** — On October 22, 2022, NEDA reported that 49% of families self-rated as poor, up from 48% in June, while attributing inflation to food, transport, global supply disruption, the Russia–Ukraine war, and calamities. The government reported targeted subsidies for low-income households, drivers, farmers, and fishers, while also acknowledging the need to accelerate assistance and food-production measures. This combines contrary household-burden evidence with an official mitigation claim. [PCO, lines 57–79](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-admin-steps-vs-rising-inflation-helped-manage-poverty-level/). Lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E050** — Marcos filed his 2022 Statement of Contributions and Expenditures, reporting approximately ₱623 million in spending and ₱624 million in contributions. The filing is an inspectable disclosure record, not proof that all contributions were lawful or fully transparent. [PNA, lines 64–82](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1176100). Lenses: `5B.7`, `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.9`. Disposition: `context`.

Shortfall: no 2022 budget-execution audit or robust household/regional causal evaluation linking outcomes to Marcos-era decisions was recovered.

### Chapter 6B — Public-service delivery

- **E051** — The 2022 Annual Poverty Indicators Survey was designed around approximately 44,000 households and was reported as reliable at national and regional levels, including information on assistance received and social-protection coverage. The accessible record was a government statistical summary; it provides a usable distributional lead but not a verified Marcos-specific improvement finding. [PSA summary](https://rssomimaropa.psa.gov.ph/content/highlights-2022-annual-poverty-indicators-survey-social-protection-programs). Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`. Disposition: `gateway_only` because the underlying page returned a retrieval restriction.

- **E052** — A 2022 education-facilities report identified 599 “Last-Mile School” classrooms targeted for construction, including schools lacking permanent structures, electricity, or potable water. Because the target and much of the budget predated Marcos’s June inauguration, this is inherited service baseline/context rather than ruler-period delivery. [PIA](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2022/04/12/deped-targets-599-classrooms-to-be-constructed-for-last-mile-school-program-in-2022). Lenses: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`. Disposition: `context`.

Shortfall: no inspectable beneficiary evaluation, regional service-quality comparison, affordability audit, or pandemic/disaster delivery assessment attributable to the six-month Marcos period was found.

### Chapter 7B — Personal integrity and conflicts

- **E053** — GMA’s review of Marcos’s Comelec SOCE reported ₱624,684,320.09 in contributions from 67 declared contributors. Anton Lagdameo was listed as the largest contributor through in-kind party support; Melquiades Robles was listed as a ₱30 million cash contributor and was appointed PCSO general manager in July 2022. These are precise financial and appointment facts; they establish a potential nexus for further review, not improper benefit or corruption. [GMA, lines 98–124](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/843268/lagdameo-listed-as-top-contributor-in-marcos-soce/story/). Lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`, `7B.9`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E054** — PCIJ’s donor review, republished by Bulatlat, reported that relatives of Marcos-era supporters, tycoons, and companies allegedly barred from political contributions helped finance the 2022 campaign. The report expressly noted that some donor identities could not be confirmed and that Comelec redacted information. This is inspectable investigative evidence of a campaign-finance nexus, not a finding of personal concealment, unlawful receipt, or post-accession benefit. [Bulatlat/PCIJ, lines 87–103](https://www.bulatlat.com/2022/08/31/data-who-donated-to-bongbong-marcos/). Lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`, `7B.9`. Disposition: `final_evidence` with allegation and attribution caveats.

Shortfall: no presidential SALN contents, beneficial-ownership trail, procurement award linkage, conflict-of-interest adjudication, correction record, or personal-benefit finding was recovered. E022 remains rejected.

### Chapter 8B — Effectiveness and implementation

- **E055** — Marcos’s transition memorandum extended holdover officials temporarily to preserve service continuity, while prohibiting new contracts, projects, and extraordinary disbursements until presidential appointments were made. This directly documents an implementation bottleneck and a continuity-control response during the transition. [Memorandum Circular No. 3](https://lawphil.net/executive/mc/mc2022/mc_3_2022.html). Lenses: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E056** — After the July 27, 2022 earthquake, DBM stated that agencies could mobilize Quick Response Funds and, subject to damage assessment and presidential approval, access the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund. This establishes a formal crisis-response mechanism and presidential approval gate; it does not verify delivery speed or adequacy. [DBM, lines 48–58](https://www.dbm.gov.ph/index.php/management-2/439-dbm-disaster-relief-budget-ready). Lenses: `8B.6`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`, `6B.6`. Disposition: `final_evidence`.

- **E057** — The 2022 DBM budget record describes prioritized agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare, rightsizing, budget modernization, and related legislative initiatives. These are formal program and resource-allocation records, but remain prospective or administrative rather than outcome evidence. [PNA report](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1191427). Lenses: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`. Disposition: `context`.

Shortfall: no independent delivery audit, coordination-failure review, personnel-performance record, or durable multi-program outcome evidence was recovered.
